title: Convert bases, pick bits apart, and pack bytes
brief: Write binary and hex conversion loops, bit masks and shifts, popcount, and little- and big-endian packing into bytes.
hints: To write n in base b, repeat: `n % b` is the next digit (lowest first), then `n //= b`. Look the digit up in the string `"0123456789abcdef"`, collect the digits, and reverse them at the end. Handle 0 on its own.
To read a digit string in base b, start with `total = 0` and for each character do `total = total * b + digit`, where `digit = "0123456789abcdef".index(ch)`.
A mask of `n` ones is `(1 << n) - 1`. `get_bits(x, lo, hi)` shifts right by `lo`, then ANDs with a mask of `hi - lo + 1` ones.
`set_bit` sets with `value | (1 << index)` and clears with `value & ~(1 << index)`.
`popcount` can loop: add `value & 1`, then shift right by one, until the value is 0.
Byte number `i`, counting from the low end, is `(value >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF`. Little-endian stores byte 0 first. Big-endian stores the same bytes in the opposite order.
`unpack_le` adds `data[i] << (8 * i)` for each index. For big-endian, reverse the bytes first (`data[::-1]`) and reuse it.
